trip.title: Costa Rica, 5 nights · 1/6–1/11
trip.subtitle: Leave the Toronto snow behind and fly south into a Pacific summer. The first night, fall asleep to the waves of Coco Bay after the sun sinks into the bay and the stars take over the beach. Then head for the hills: past a waterfall tucked in the forest and up into misty Monteverde, to fly more than a kilometre above the treetops; after dark, follow a flashlight into the rainforest and listen to it wake. The last three nights are at the foot of Arenal Volcano, hot springs right outside the door: drift down a river past caimans sunning on the banks, ride out to see the volcano, and follow a guide to find a sloth taking its time in the branches.
trip.notice: Flights (PD 783 out, PD 7301 back), all three hotels and the Dollar rental car are booked; the car is still awaiting confirmation from Dollar. Flights and hotels were re-checked on Nov 15–16 for this version of the route; the rental car is Dollar's actual price, with Adobe and Alamo kept as backups (own-site quotes from 11/19). USD converted at the Bank of Canada rate of 2026-11-13 (1 USD = 1.4257 CAD); Costa Rica VAT is 13%. January is the local school holiday, so beaches are still fairly busy around 1/6.
constraints: No surfing. Her Achilles is in late-stage rehab (already jogging and doing weight training), so regular tours are fine; just take a little care on rocky paths, getting on and off boats, and horseback riding
Driver is 23 at time of travel · Canadian G licence
Rental car must be an SUV; the smallest SUV is fine
Finish long and mountain drives in daylight (sunset ~17:30); at night only short drives of a few km in town

days.title: Wed · Nonstop to Liberia, sunset and stars on the beach in Coco

schedule.title: Arrive at Pearson Terminal 3
schedule.text: Arrive 3 hours early for international flights. Partner: bring Chinese passport, US visa (confirm it's multiple-entry, M) and PR card.

schedule.title: Porter PD 783 Toronto → Liberia
schedule.text: About 5h 44m nonstop. Departure is Toronto time, landing is local time (1 hour behind Toronto). After landing, get the entry stamp (check it's in your passport), collect bags, then head to the Dollar shuttle stop.

schedule.title: Pick up the car
schedule.text: Bring your physical licence, passport, and a credit card in the driver's name (deposit ~USD1,000). Inspect the car and take photos; check by hand that the doors are locked, as rental car break-ins are common here.

schedule.title: Check in at Playas del Coco
schedule.text: About 35 min from the Dollar office, arrive before dark.

schedule.title: Sunset on the beach
schedule.text: The beach in front of the hotel faces west, so the sun sets right over the water.

schedule.title: Seafood by the sea
schedule.text: Walk into Coco town (about 15 minutes): Papagayo Seafood (often live music) or Mar Azul; take a taxi back if you don’t feel like walking.

schedule.title: Stargazing on the beach
schedule.text: Tomorrow, 1/7, is the new moon, so tonight is nearly moonless; Guanacaste’s dry season is mostly clear and it is fully dark by 19:00. The darker north end of Coco beach is right in front of the hotel; walk away from the streetlights, lie on a towel and look: Orion is high in the southeast with Sirius, the brightest star, below it; after 21:00 look low in the south for Canopus (the second-brightest star, never visible from Toronto). Use Stellarium or SkyView on your phone to identify stars. Bring only your phone and a towel, no valuables, and don’t wander far; tomorrow is an early start on mountain roads, so don’t stay up too late.

days.title: Thu · A waterfall on the way, flying over the cloud forest, a night walk in the rainforest

schedule.title: Check out and set off
schedule.text: Bring some cash (the waterfall is cash only). South via Liberia and Bagaces, about 1 h 15 min to the waterfall.

schedule.title: Llanos de Cortés waterfall
schedule.text: About 30 concrete steps with a rope handrail; sandy at the bottom, rocky at the edge and in the water. You can take a dip; watch your step on the rocks so you don't roll an ankle.

schedule.title: Route 1 to Monteverde
schedule.text: Via Cañas, turning onto Route 606 for the climb, about 2.5 hours; Route 606 is paved but steep with tight bends, so take it slowly. Reach Santa Elena around 12:00 for a quick lunch.

schedule.title: 100% Aventura ziplines
schedule.text: About 2.5–3 hours: 10 ziplines, the longest 1,590 m, the longest in Costa Rica; the last two are Superman lines you fly face-down, plus one Tarzan swing (optional). From USD72 per person on the official site (plus tax), transport not included; about 10 minutes’ drive from town. Check the booking page for slots (commonly 8:00, 11:00, 13:00, 15:00). Her Achilles is still in rehab: on the Superman lines staff brake you and help you stand, so the stop itself is gentle; what to watch is the stairs and forest paths between platforms, and the occasional foot touchdown at the end of the regular lines, so ask her physio before booking.

links.label: Alternative: Selvatura ziplines (also has a Superman line)

schedule.title: Check in to the Monteverde hotel
schedule.text: 0.8 km from the town centre; rest a bit and grab a jacket: Monteverde evenings are only in the teens and often windy with drizzle.

schedule.title: Rainforest night walk
schedule.text: At Bajo del Tigre (Children’s Eternal Rainforest) a guide leads you by flashlight to find tree frogs, snakes, spiders and sleeping birds, and with luck sloths and agoutis. USD30 + tax per person, minimum 2; about 5 minutes’ drive from the hotel. The trails are forest dirt paths, so wear closed non-slip shoes and bring a rain jacket and bug spray.

links.label: Bajo del Tigre rates and booking
Alternative: Monteverde Cloud Forest Reserve night walk

schedule.title: Dinner in town
schedule.text: Eat in Santa Elena town, then drive a few minutes back to the hotel.

days.title: Fri · Down the mountain and around the lake to the volcano, hot springs in the afternoon

schedule.title: Breakfast
schedule.text: Breakfast is included at the hotel; mornings in the mountains are the clearest, with cloud rising out of the valleys.

schedule.title: Down to La Fortuna
schedule.text: Down Route 606, via Cañas and Tilarán, then along the north shore of Lake Arenal; all paved, about 4 hours of driving. Skip the dirt shortcut from Monteverde to Tilarán.

schedule.title: North shore of Lake Arenal
schedule.text: Follow the winding Route 142 and stop at roadside viewpoints for photos of the lake and volcano; lunch in Nuevo Arenal.

schedule.title: Check in at Termales del Arenal
schedule.text: All the driving done in daylight. Once the room is ready, start with the hotel hot spring pools.

schedule.title: Soak in the hotel hot springs
schedule.text: Soak for a while, then head into town for dinner in the evening.

alternatives.title: Rainforest Chocolate Tour (15:00)
alternatives.text: In La Fortuna town, about 2 hours: see cacao trees, grind the beans yourself and taste fresh hot chocolate. Mostly flat, with plenty of sitting. English tours at 8:00, 10:00, 13:00 and 15:00, about USD34 per person (about CA$97 for two). About 10 minutes’ drive from the hotel; have dinner in town afterwards.

schedule.title: Souvenir shopping in town
schedule.text: Do a loop around the central park; everything is within 150 m. Cianikal is a local artists' collective with volcanic-stone and silver jewellery, ceramics, prints and small-batch chocolate (daily 9:00–21:00). Lava Collective in the park has local handmade cups, honey and coffee (12:00–20:00). Galería Onírica, north of the church, sells original paintings and jade, at higher prices. For coffee to take home, Mega Súper two blocks southwest of the park (7:00–21:00) is cheaper than the gift shops. Walk on to dinner afterwards and leave the car in town.

schedule.title: Dinner in town
schedule.text: Snapper's House is right in the town centre; drive 5 minutes back to the hotel afterwards.

days.title: Sat · River float for sloths and crocodiles, hanging bridges in the afternoon

schedule.title: Early volcano viewing
schedule.text: The volcano is most likely to show itself 6–9 am, and you can see it from the hotel.

schedule.title: Peñas Blancas safari float
schedule.text: Hotel pickup; you sit in an inflatable raft steered by the guide, with little or no paddling (some operators ask for a few light strokes), for about 2 hours spotting sloths, monkeys, caimans and birds; back around 11:00. You get on and off at the riverbank, which may be muddy and rocky, so watch your step and wear non-slip, closed-toe water shoes.

links.label: Fortuna Welcome safari float · USD70 with transfers · leaves 7:30, about 4 hours
Alternative: Desafío safari float · USD72 + tax with transfers · starts 8:00, about 3 hours, some light paddling
Alternative: Two Weeks in Costa Rica safari float · USD69 + tax from January, with transfers · leaves 7:30, about 4.5 hours

schedule.title: Lunch in town
schedule.text: Ceviche at Cevichería D'Mora.

schedule.title: Mistico Hanging Bridges Park
schedule.text: About 25 min drive. 3.2 km loop with gentle slopes and steps; the hanging bridges sway; ~2 hours. Tag along behind a guided group and you'll often spot small creatures like eyelash vipers. Watch your footing on the slopes. Last entry 15:50.

links.label: Alternative: Mistico guided natural history walk · USD44 + tax · about 2.5 hours, a guide spots wildlife for you
Alternative: Fortuna Welcome hanging bridges tour · USD70 with transfers and entry · leaves 14:00, about 4 hours
Alternative: Sky Adventures hanging bridges (El Castillo, about 40 minutes by car) · booking required

schedule.title: Back to the hotel for the hot springs
schedule.text: After the bridges, soak for a while before heading out to dinner.

alternatives.title: Rest at the hotel, or stroll the town centre
alternatives.text: If you skip the hot springs after the bridges, rest in the room for a bit; around sunset walk to the little park in front of the church in town, with the volcano straight ahead, grab a coffee, then go to dinner.

schedule.title: Dinner in town
schedule.text: 5 min drive to town: Snapper's House (marlin ceviche, seafood soup) or Cevichería D'Mora; drive back to the hotel afterwards.

days.title: Sun · Horseback to the volcano in the morning, sloths in the afternoon

schedule.title: Hotel pickup (horseback tour)
schedule.text: The volcano is most likely to be visible in the morning.

schedule.title: Horseback ride with Arenal Volcano views
schedule.text: About 2.5 hours of riding through forest and pasture to a volcano viewpoint and Los Lirios lake; the guide gives a lesson first. Note: keeping heels down in the stirrups and pushing off one foot to mount and dismount put some strain on the Achilles; if it feels tight, keep the horse at a walk.

links.label: Alternative: Mistico Paco’s Horses ride · USD58 + tax · starts 8:15, about 2.5 hours, crosses a river on horseback
Alternative: Don Tobias ride to a volcano lookout · starts 8:30, about 3 hours, transfers included, ask for the price

schedule.title: Back to the hotel to change and have lunch
schedule.text: A simple lunch at the hotel or in town; the sloth tour picks you up at 13:00.

schedule.title: Sloth tour
schedule.text: A guide leads you along gentle trails through farm forest looking for sloths, often both two- and three-toed, plus birds, frogs and hummingbirds; about 2.5–3 hours, rated "easy", hotel pickup included. USD90 per person incl. tax, minimum 2 people.

links.label: Alternative: Fortuna Welcome sloths + farm lunch (about 6 hours)

alternatives.title: Rainforest Chocolate Tour (13:00)
alternatives.text: About 2 hours, USD34 per person: see cacao trees, grind the beans yourself and taste hot chocolate; then rest at the hotel.

alternatives.title: Soak and rest at the hotel
alternatives.text: Stay in and spend the afternoon in the hotel hot spring pools, then go into town for dinner.

schedule.title: Dinner at the hotel
schedule.text: Eat at the hotel, or drive 5 minutes into town.

days.title: Mon · Drive back to Liberia, nonstop flight home

schedule.title: One last look at the volcano, breakfast
A slow morning
schedule.text: The flight isn’t until the afternoon, so soak in the hotel hot springs once more and check out by 10:00.

schedule.title: Head to the airport
schedule.text: Along the lake via Tilarán and Cañas, about 3 hours on the road; allow time to fill up (the car must be returned full) and arrive by 13:15.

schedule.title: Return the car, shuttle to the airport
schedule.text: The departure tax is usually included in the airfare. The return is operated by Air Transat, so check in and drop bags at the Air Transat counter; arriving 2.5–3 hours before an international flight is safest.

schedule.title: Porter PD 7301 nonstop back to Toronto
schedule.text: Operated by Air Transat, about 5 h 10 min, arriving at Pearson at 22:45. Partner shows PR card when entering Canada.

coverage.note: About 530 steps down, and the climb back up is harder; not great value just for a look at the falls.

coverage.item: Arenal 1968 lava trails / national park trails
coverage.note: These are hiking trails; enjoying volcano views from the lake and the hotel instead.

coverage.item: Rincón de la Vieja mud bath and hot springs
coverage.note: About 1 hour from Coco; on this version 1/7 is the drive to Monteverde, so it doesn’t fit.

coverage.item: Palo Verde boat tour for crocodiles
coverage.note: Overlaps with the Peñas Blancas float; private tour USD178 + tax, fairly pricey.
Day passes are suspended through 1/5 for the Christmas season and available from 1/6; the hotel’s own hot springs are enough.
No surfing; Tamarindo is 1.5 hours from the airport and mostly about surfing and nightlife.
Same route; flights with carry-on cost about CA$670 more, but hotels like Villa del Sueño have availability.
Termales del Arenal has its own hot-spring pools and is right next door to Ecotermales; for a change of scene, go during the day (10:00–16:00 session).

coverage.item: Bogarín night walk / daytime sloth trail
coverage.when: Replaced by the Monteverde night walk and sloth tour
coverage.note: The night wildlife walk is in Monteverde (the cloud forest has different species from the volcano side); sloths are on the 1/10 afternoon sloth tour.

coverage.item: Other spots from the RedNote posts
coverage.note: Poás Volcano, La Paz Waterfall Gardens and the Starbucks coffee farm are near San José, 2–3 hours from La Fortuna; Maquique canyoning and Finca Modelo tree climbing don’t suit Achilles rehab; Monteverde gets one night in this version: 100% Aventura ziplines + a night walk.

Late-stage rehab, already jogging and doing weight training: regular tours are all in; rocky paths, horseback riding and the ziplines are marked "take care" in the itinerary, and she should ask her physio before booking the ziplines. La Fortuna Waterfall (about 530 steps, mixed reviews in the post) is not included.

The long legs (airport to Coco, Coco to Monteverde, Monteverde to the volcano, volcano back to the airport) are all in daylight; at night only a few minutes’ driving in town (Coco, Santa Elena, La Fortuna).
To fit 100% Aventura in Monteverde, Coco is down to one night; January is Papagayo wind season with strong afternoon winds, so boat trips depend on the weather anyway.
The hotel has its own hot spring pools to use any time over three nights; the 1/10 afternoon is now the sloth tour.
You’re already doing 100% Aventura in Monteverde (with Superman lines), so no repeat.

rental.title: Car rental: pick up 1/6 16:15 – return 1/11 13:15 (5 days)
rental.summary: There's no convenient public transit between the two regions, so we drive all five days. Booked: a Dollar SUV (Subaru Crosstrek or similar) through Booking.com, still awaiting confirmation; the office is about 2 km from Liberia airport with a shuttle. Adobe's and Alamo's quotes stay as backups.

details.label: Driver
details.value: 23 at time of travel, Canadian G licence (whether Dollar charges a young-driver fee is on the confirmation)

details.label: Pick-up / return
details.value: Dollar's Liberia airport office (about 2 km outside the airport, shuttle)

details.label: Default vehicle
details.value: Subaru Crosstrek or similar SUV, CA$710.01 (Booking.com total)

details.label: Current status
details.value: Booked · awaiting Dollar confirmation; check whether mandatory third-party liability is included

notes: Mandatory third-party liability (TPL/SLI) can't be waived, and most low prices on third-party sites exclude it; go by the rental office's quote.

Other companies: Vamos also has no young-driver fee; Europcar charges USD6/day; Alamo's own site charges a USD50 young-driver fee for the whole rental at 23 (the Alamo option stays in the budget as a backup); Enterprise and National charge drivers aged 21–24 but don't publish the amount.
A Canadian licence is valid as is; bring your original passport (copies aren't accepted).
Leave nothing in the car, and after parking pull the door handle to confirm it's locked (thieves sometimes jam key-fob signals).
Drive the long legs in daylight: sunset is around 17:30, Route 142 along the lake is winding and dark, and Route 606 up to Monteverde is steep with tight bends; at night only short drives in town.

events.title: 1/7 new moon · stargazing
events.description: The nights of 1/6–1/10 are nearly moonless. Guanacaste’s dry season is mostly clear: look from the north end of the beach in front of the Coco hotel on 1/6; on 1/7 look up during the Monteverde night walk, though the mountains are often cloudy; and on the volcano nights, from the hot spring pools.
events.conflict: No driving: walk to the beach in front of the hotel; bring only your phone and a towel.

events.title: Santa Cruz / Palmares festivals
events.description: The Santa Cruz traditional festival is usually 1/14–1/18, and the Palmares festival runs mid-to-late January; both are after this trip.

items.title: Confirm your Canadian passport is valid for the whole trip
items.note: Canadian citizens are visa-free for up to 180 days; make sure you get an entry stamp in your passport. Bring your return itinerary.

The official site couldn't be fetched automatically, so check the immigration page in a browser before departure or ask the airline.

cash.summary: Hotels, tours, gas stations and most restaurants take cards (Visa/Mastercard). Cash is only needed for the items below: US dollars mainly for tips and emergencies, colones for small places that only take local currency. Most of it is already counted in the food and tickets budgets; tips of about US$45 come out of the buffer.

currencies.label: US dollars
currencies.how: Exchange CAD at a Canadian bank or currency exchange before leaving. Get small, crisp, undamaged bills (damaged US bills are often refused locally): $1×10, $5×6, $10×3, $20×4.

currencies.label: Costa Rican colones
currencies.how: Don't exchange in Canada. After landing, withdraw about ₡30,000 from a bank ATM (BCR, BN, BAC) in the Liberia Airport arrivals hall or in Coco or La Fortuna; some ATMs don't work from 11 pm to 5 am.

items.label: Llanos de Cortés waterfall entry
items.note: ₡4,000 per person, cash only (1/7)

items.label: Parking attendants (cuidacarros)
items.note: Informal attendants watch cars at beaches and on town streets, ₡500–1,000 each time

items.label: Sodas, fruit stands, ice cream
items.note: Small shops may not take cards; already in the food budget

items.label: Evening taxi in Coco (optional)
items.note: Taxi from town back to Villa Del Sol if you don't feel like walking, about ₡2,000 per ride

items.label: Tips for guides and crew
items.note: About US$10 each for the zipline, float and sloth guides

items.label: Housekeeping tips
items.note: About US$2/night × 5 nights; restaurant bills already include a 10% service charge, so no extra tip needed

items.label: Emergency cash
items.note: For when cards or ATMs don't work; bring it home if unused

tips: Exchange rate about ₡450 = US$1 (Nov 2026); US$1 is about 1.4257 CAD (Bank of Canada, 11/13).
US dollars are accepted everywhere, but change often comes back in colones at a poor rate; paying in colones at small places is better value.
When the card machine asks whether to pay in CAD or colones, choose colones (local currency); don't let the merchant convert it to CAD.
Use a credit card with no foreign transaction fee; ATM withdrawals charge a fee, so take out enough at once rather than several times.
